title: Rabbi Nechunya
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Chullin 55b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.55b) he said: “I asked all the experts in the laws of trefot (those who rule on the laws of animals unfit for consumption) in the West, and they told me: the halakhah follows Rekhish bar Pappa, and the halakhah does not follow Rav Avira in the name of Rava.” (Apparently he was one of the sages who went down from the Land of Israel to Babylonia toward the end of the time of Abaye and Rava.) This Rabbi Nechunya is mentioned in [Bava Kamma 50a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.50a): “Rabbi Nechunya said: from here,” etc.[^1]

notes.text: The gloss explaining the experts in trefot and the parenthetical historical inference are Hyman’s own. The inference remains qualified as “apparently.” א״י and ב״ק are the ordinary contextual abbreviations for the Land of Israel and Bava Kamma. The printed locators נה: and נ. are rendered as 55b and 50a by the conventional colon/period notation; neither passage has been independently verified here.
